# Example transcript: running s07 (GitRepo + auto-commit).
#
# This is an ILLUSTRATIVE run, not a byte-exact fixture. SHAs are random, so the
# exact "committed <sha>" hash differs every run; what the tests pin is the
# BEHAVIOR (one new commit, the message, the author attribution, the no-empty-
# commit guard). For a hand run, what matters is the SHAPE shown below.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Set up a throwaway git repo to play in. (The tests do this automatically
#    with t.TempDir(); here we do it by hand.)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ mkdir /tmp/demo && cd /tmp/demo && git init -q
$ git config user.name "Ada Lovelace"
$ git config user.email "ada@example.com"
$ printf 'package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n' > app.go
$ git add app.go && git commit -q -m "initial"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Apply a whole-file edit and AUTO-COMMIT it. No network, no API key.
#    This is the core demo: edit -> commit -> new sha, all in one command.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run /path/to/agents/s07-gitrepo-autocommit \
      -repo /tmp/demo -file app.go \
      -content 'package main

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("hello from aider") }
' -m "print a greeting" -v
[s07] repo root: /tmp/demo
[s07] wrote 78 bytes to app.go
[s07] committed a1b2c3d: print a greeting
committed a1b2c3d

# The edit is now an atomic, attributed git commit. Inspect it like any other:
$ git log --oneline -1
a1b2c3d print a greeting
$ git log -1 --pretty='%an <%ae>'
Ada Lovelace (aider) <ada@example.com>
#                ^^^^^^^ author NAME rewritten to mark this as aider's work
#                        (the email is untouched — only the display name).

# Undo it the aider way — the commit IS the undo buffer:
$ git reset --hard HEAD~1     # this is what aider's /undo runs

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Re-running with NO actual change is a no-op. aider never makes empty
#    "noise" commits, so a clean tree just reports and skips.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run /path/to/agents/s07-gitrepo-autocommit \
      -repo /tmp/demo -file app.go -content "$(cat app.go)" -v
[s07] repo root: /tmp/demo
[s07] wrote 78 bytes to app.go
[s07] no changes to commit (clean tree) — skipping
committed (no commit: nothing changed)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. The kinder-to-blame attribution: keep the human as author, tag the model
#    in a Co-authored-by trailer instead of rewriting the name.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ printf '// touched\n' >> app.go
$ go run /path/to/agents/s07-gitrepo-autocommit \
      -repo /tmp/demo -file app.go -content "$(cat app.go)" \
      -m "add a comment" -co-authored-by -model claude-sonnet-4-6
committed e4f5a6b
$ git log -1 --pretty='%B'
add a comment

Co-authored-by: aider (claude-sonnet-4-6) <aider@aider.chat>
$ git log -1 --pretty='%an'
Ada Lovelace
#             ^ author NAME is the human now; the trailer credits the model.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. RUN mode (optional, needs a key): let a model produce the new contents,
#    then auto-commit them. The reply is non-deterministic; the commit step is
#    identical to the offline demos above.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
$ go run /path/to/agents/s07-gitrepo-autocommit \
      -repo /tmp/demo -file app.go \
      -instruction "rename the greeting to 'hi there'" -v
[s07] repo root: /tmp/demo
[s07] asking claude-sonnet-4-6 for new contents of app.go
[s07] wrote 81 bytes to app.go
[s07] committed 7c8d9e0: edit app.go
committed 7c8d9e0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. The tests (no network — they drive real git in a temp repo).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go test -v ./...
=== RUN   TestCommitCreatesOneCommit
--- PASS: TestCommitCreatesOneCommit
=== RUN   TestCommitMessageRecorded
--- PASS: TestCommitMessageRecorded
=== RUN   TestCommitAttributionAuthor
--- PASS: TestCommitAttributionAuthor
=== RUN   TestNoEmptyCommitAndIsDirty
--- PASS: TestNoEmptyCommitAndIsDirty
=== RUN   TestTrackedFilesAndRootFromSubdir
--- PASS: TestTrackedFilesAndRootFromSubdir
PASS
ok  	learn-aider/s07
